ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, in the cross-sectional view of a certain transparent medium, $\triangle A O C$ is an isosceles right triangle, $B C$ is a quarter-circle arc with radius $R=10\mathrm{cm}$, and AB is perpendicular to the horizontal screen MN and contacts it at point $A$. A composite light consisting of red and violet monochromatic lights is directed towards the center $o$, with an incident angle $i=45^{\circ}$ at the interface AB, resulting in two bright spots appearing on the horizontal screen MN. It is known that the refractive indices of the medium for red and violet lights are $n_{1}=\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}$ and $n_{2}=\sqrt{2}$, respectively.

1. Determine the colors of the bright spots produced at locations AM and AN.
2. What is the distance between the two bright spots?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
AM red; AN a mixture of red and purple
(5\sqrt{2}+10)\mathrm{{cm}}

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: At the top of the figure is a horizontal screen MN, point A is located on the screen, AB goes vertically downward from A, and is perpendicular to the screen MN. Point O is on AB, and B is below O. Point C is to the right of O, AC is the hypotenuse connected from A toward the lower right to C, and BC is a quarter circular arc with O as the center. The incident composite light is directed from the lower right toward the circular arc BC, and points to the center O; in the figure, the angle of incidence i=45° is marked near O. Reasoning: Establish a coordinate system according to the figure, take O=(0,0), A=(0,R), B=(0,-R), C=(R,0), the horizontal screen MN is y=R, and the equation of the inclined plane AC is x+y=R. Since the incident light is directed toward the center O, and BC is a circular arc with O as the center, the light ray is incident along the normal on the circular arc surface BC, is not refracted when entering the medium, and reaches point O on the surface AB. AB is a vertical interface, whose normal is horizontal, and the problem gives the angle of incidence at AB as i=45°. When red light travels from the medium to air, use the law of refraction: sin r = n1 sin i = (2√3/3)(√2/2)=√6/3. Thus cos r=√3/3, tan r=√2. After the red light is refracted from O into the air on the left side, it reaches the upper screen; the vertical distance OA=R, so the horizontal distance on the left screen is AM=R/tan r=10/√2=5√2 cm. Therefore there is a red-light bright spot at AM. For violet light, n2=√2, and n2 sin45°=√2·√2/2=1, that is, it just reaches the critical condition, so ordinary refracted light does not form a bright spot on the left screen. At the same time, at the AB surface, both kinds of light have reflected components; after reflection, the light ray travels from O in the upper-right 45° direction, exactly perpendicular to the inclined plane AC, so it is not refracted when exiting at AC. This light ray continues along the same straight line to reach the horizontal screen y=R, and from the geometric relation its landing point is at a distance AN=R=10 cm to the right of A. Therefore at AN there are both red light and violet light, that is, a red-violet mixed bright spot. The two bright spots are respectively 5√2 cm to the left of A and 10 cm to the right of A, so the distance between them is AM+AN=5√2+10 cm.
